title: Split+
tagline: Split parts, surfaces, curves or faces at a start tool and an optional end tool. Pieces are named inside / outside (start, end) from geometry you pick, so the side to keep does not depend on any normal.

slides.title: What it does
slides.problem: The built-in Split keeps "front" or "back" of one tool. That choice is tied to the tool's normal, which flips whenever an upstream loft, offset, mirror or sketch changes. Split+ cuts at a start tool and an optional end tool and names every piece inside or outside -- with an inside reference, inside is the side of each tool that reference is on.
useWhen: A body must be cut by two planes or surfaces in one step
You keep the inside or the outside, and the tools' normals may change upstream
Later features need the pieces by name: inside, start, end
slides.caption: Split+ open on a ski topsheet: the target and the two tools (Station A = start tool, B = end tool) highlight.

slides.title: Why a reference instead of a flip

points.head: A flip is about a normal
points.body: 'Keep front' means the side the tool's normal points to -- and normals change freely upstream.

points.head: A reference is about the model
points.body: Pick geometry on the side you mean. The choice survives any change of orientation.

points.head: Drop-in
points.body: With one tool and no reference, inside is the tool's front, as in the built-in Split (an info notice says so).

points.head: Signed distance
points.body: For each tool: s = (P - C) . n at the closest point. s > 0: the reference is in front of the tool.

points.head: Inside = the reference's side of every tool
points.body: With an inside reference, inside is the side of each tool it is on; outside is everything else.

points.head: No reference
points.body: Two tools: inside is between the cuts. One tool: inside is the tool's front (info notice).

points.head: Start tool, optional end tool
points.body: Start = beyond the start tool, end = beyond the end tool, outside = start + end. Inside is what is on the inside of every tool.

points.head: Orientation never matters
points.body: The names follow the reference (or the other tool), not the normals, and not the order Onshape returns several tools in.

points.head: Crossing tools
points.body: A piece beyond both tools counts as outside only (in neither start nor end), with an info notice.

slides.title: The dialog: split, keep both
params: Split type
PART: split whole bodies. FACE: split only the picked faces; nothing is removed.
Parts, surfaces, or curves to split
The targets. Every target is split by the tools.
Start tool
A surface, face, plane or mate connector. What lies beyond it is the start region; its cut is startCut.
End tool
Optional second cut (endCut). Inside is then between the two tools.
Inside reference
Geometry in the region you call inside. Needed with one tool to name the sides.
Bodies to keep
Both (default): every piece is kept and sorted into regions. Inside / Outside: the other region is deleted (next slide).
Trim to face boundaries
A single-face tool cuts only within its own boundary, as the built-in.
Keep tools
Keep sheet-body tools after the split.

slides.title: The dialog: keep inside only
params: Bodies to keep
Inside: the pieces on the inside of every tool survive; the rest is deleted. Outside: the reverse.
Inside reference
Geometry inside the region you want -- best a mate connector or vertex. Here: Mid (x 900).
Debug
Print sides: which side of each tool is inside and how that was decided, and the pieces of each region.
slides.note: Result: only the region between Station A and B survives, whatever way the two planes face (example 2).

slides.title: The dialog: face split
params: Split type
FACE: split only the picked faces. Nothing is removed; the pieces stay part of their body.
Faces to split
The faces to split. Planes and mate connectors cut them infinitely; surfaces cut as they are.
Inside reference
Optional. With one tool it names the inside / outside regions; it never removes anything here.
slides.note: Regions are published as faces: pick 'inside' in Extract variables to fillet or offset only those faces.

slides.title: Example 1: three regions
slides.head: Topsheet split at Station A (x 300, start tool) and B (x 1500, end tool), Bodies to keep: Both
slides.body: Nothing is removed. The three pieces are published as start (x -19..300), inside (300..1500) and end (1500..1799), and the cut edges as splitEdges -- one edge per cut: 9 edges, 5 at A and 4 at B.

slides.title: Example 2: keep only the middle
slides.head: VOLUME_STD split at Station A and B, Bodies to keep: Inside, Inside reference = Mid (x 900)
slides.body: Inside is the side of each station plane that Mid is on, so only the part between A and B survives (green); the tip and tail pieces (grey) are removed. Flipping either plane's normal changes nothing -- which the built-in 'keep front / back' cannot promise.

slides.title: Example 3: split faces, not bodies
slides.head: Face split: the SW_SHELF faces (the shelf along the sidewall) cut at Station A and B
slides.body: Nothing is removed and no new body is made: the shelf faces are divided at A and B and published as regions -- start 4 faces, inside 9, end 4. A later feature (a fillet, an offset, a Thicken+) can then work on 'inside' alone, and keeps working when the stations move.

slides.title: Outputs: what Extract variables can publish
keys: The pieces kept (faces in a Face split).
The pieces in each region: bodies (solids, surfaces or curves) in a Part split, faces in a Face split. outside = start + end (and any piece beyond both tools).
A region's edges except the cuts (for a surface: its open boundary).
The cut each tool made: the edge on a kept piece (the inside piece, or the outside piece when keeping only outside). Topsheet example: startCut = the 5 edges at x 300.
Every cut: one edge per cut, on a kept piece. Keeping both sides leaves two coincident copies of every cut edge; only one is published. Input edges that were merely cut in two are not included.
The cap faces the split created on solids (empty for surfaces and in a Face split).
Number: the pieces kept. Every key is always present, empty when it does not apply.

slides.title: Messages
messages: The start and end tools are the same / A tool is also a target
Pick a different end tool; pick each body only once, as target or tool.
The inside reference lies on the start / end tool
The reference has no side of that tool. Move it clearly to one side.
The start and end tools meet or cross ... pick an inside reference
Without a reference, 'between' is not defined.
Nothing is left: no piece lies inside / outside
Inside is the start tool's front ... / N piece(s) lie beyond both tools
One tool and no reference: the names follow the tool's normal. Crossing tools: such pieces count as outside, in neither start nor end.

items.head: Use a local reference
items.body: A mate connector or vertex inside the region you call inside. A far plane can read the wrong side where the part curves.

items.head: Start tool first
items.body: Start = beyond the start tool; the optional end tool gives end. Region names follow which tool is which.

items.head: Reference regions, not indices
items.body: Extract variables can publish 'inside' or 'startCut'; those names survive changes upstream.

items.head: Outputs keep their input's orientation
items.body: The reference picks the side to keep, not the normal: pieces face the way the input faced (the topsheet example faces down). Built-ins downstream (Thicken, Offset surface, Move face) follow that normal -- put Orient to reference before them, or use Thicken+ / Offset+.

items.head: Edge tools are not offered
items.body: The side rule needs a surface. Use the built-in Split for projected edges.

items.head: How pieces are sorted into regions
items.body: Split+ checks which side of each tool one point of each piece lies on (a point on one of its faces). A piece that curls back across a tool's extended plane could land in the wrong region -- check regions with Show in Extract variables.
